row.name: Precious Angels Day Care & Learning Center

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Criteria for Extreme Weather: Operational policies were reviewed and are missing the following information:    (18)(F) Outdoor play weather criteria,  (23)(a) how parents may access minimum standards online,  (23)(c) how parents may access HHS website,  (26)(b) Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of issues regarding child abuse and neglect,  (26)(c) Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness ofprevention techniques for child abuse and neglect,  (26)(d) Strategies for coordination between the center and appropriate community organizations,  (26)(e) Actions that the parent of a child who is a victim of abuse or neglect should take to obtain assistance and intervention,  (28) Information on vaccine-preventable diseases for employees and,  (30) Procedures for supporting inclusive services to children with special care needs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Criteria for Extreme Weather (26 TAC §746.501(a)(18)(F))

occurrences.finding: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Not expired or damaged in accident: Two out three car seats in the transportation van expired 12/2015. Note: this was corrected at inspection when expired seats were removed from transportation vehicle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Not expired or damaged in accident (26 TAC §746.5607(b))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: There are multiple missing floor tiles in the kitchen and dinning room. There is a hole in the wall by the nursery 1 room. Restroom by nursery 1 has chipping paint. Diaper changing mat in the prek room was torn. Fence surrounding the AC units fell over on one side.     Note: diaper changing mat was replaced during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training: Based on the information obtained during the course of the investigation, two staff members are missing 16 hours of pre-service training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance: Based on the information obtained during the course of the investigation, attendance records for two staff members were not recorded / available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance (26 TAC §746.801(5))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: Based on the information obtained during the course of the investigation, one caregiver was left in charge of supervising six infants (SAG 0-12mo) during naptime / lunch breaks.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment - Crib for Each Non-walking Infant Younger Than 12 Months of Age: Based on the information obtained during the course of the investigation, a non-walking infant under the age of 12 months did not have an individual crib to sleep in.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment - Crib for Each Non-walking Infant Younger Than 12 Months of Age (26 TAC §746.2405(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Children's Records: There was no record available for review for a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Children's Records (26 TAC §746.801(1))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: Screen time was provided to a group of children of varying ages including infants in the cafeteria area.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Play Yards - Snug Fitting, Firm, Flat Mattress Designed for Use in Play Yard and No Extra Pads: Two play yards used by infants have a mattress that was not firm and flat. There are gaps between the mattress and the play yard sides.      Note: The caregiver secured the mattress by placing the mattress pad's Velcro tabs through the slits on the play yard.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Play Yards - Snug Fitting, Firm, Flat Mattress Designed for Use in Play Yard and No Extra Pads (26 TAC §746.2411(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A school-aged child was observed unsupervised in the after school room located at the entrance of the center. The rest of the children and staff were in the kitchen/cafeteria area waiting for breakfast.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: Written feeding instructions were not available for an infant not ready for table food. The written feeding instructions for a second infant were not current. The date on the feeding instructions form was March 2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies reviewed were missing the following information:    (1) Procedures for suspension and expulsion of children;    (2) Hearing and vision screening requirements;    (3) The Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity that is consistent with Subchapter F of this chapter (relating to Developmental Activities and Activity   Plan); policies must include:  (A) The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play;  (B) The duration of physical activity at your operation, both indoor and outdoor;  (C) The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation;  (D) Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place;  (E) The recommended clothing and footwear that will allow a child to participate freely and safely in physical activities; and  (F) A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.    (4) Procedures for parents to participate in the child-care center s operation and activities.    (5) Procedures for parents to review a copy of the child-care center's most recent Licensing inspection report and how the parent may access the minimum standards online;    (6) Instructions on how a parent may contact the local Licensing office, and access the HHSC website;    (7) ) Preventing and responding to abuse and neglect of children, including:    (B)Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of issues regarding child abuse and neglect, including warning signs that a child may be a victim of abuse or neglect and factors indicating a child is at risk for abuse or neglect;    (C)Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of prevention techniques for child abuse and neglect; and    (D) Strategies for coordination between the center and appropriate community organizations;    (8) Procedures for conducting health checks;    (9) Information on vaccine-preventable diseases for employees.

Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Three of Five caregiver training records reivewed were missing annual training in Preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, including immunizations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: Two of Five personnel records reviewed were missing documentation showing how the caregivers meet the education qualifications, and a notarized Licensing Affidavit for Applicants for Employment form.
Children's Records Maintained: One of Six childrens imunization records reviewed was not current. One of Six childrens records reivewed was missing the health care provider statement.
Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent: Daily reports were not available for 4 infants in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent (26 TAC §746.2431)
